title.en: The Basic Structure: How Parliament's Amending Power Found Its Limit
title.hi: मूल ढांचा: संसद की संशोधन शक्ति और उसकी सीमा

sources.name: Constitution of India, Article 368 (text as printed, Indian Kanoon)
sources.what: Amending power, special majority, ratification by half the States for listed provisions, clause 3 excluding Article 13, clauses 4 and 5 still printed

sources.name: Sri Sankari Prasad Singh Deo v Union of India, 5 October 1951, 1952 SCR 89
sources.what: First Amendment (Arts 31A, 31B) upheld; amendments are not 'law' under Article 13(2); five-judge bench

sources.name: I.C. Golaknath v State of Punjab, 27 February 1967, 1967 SCR (2) 762
sources.what: Eleven judges, majority of six (five plus Hidayatullah J); amendment is 'law' under Art 13(2); fundamental rights cannot be abridged; prospective overruling; Sajjan Singh (1964) and Seventeenth Amendment; Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act

sources.name: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala, 24 April 1973
sources.what: Thirteen judges; Kerala land reform petition of 1970; challenge to 24th, 25th, 29th Amendments; Sikri CJ's list of basic features; Shelat and Grover JJ: 'These cannot be catalogued but can only be illustrated'

sources.name: Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain, 7 November 1975
sources.what: Allahabad HC judgment of 12 June 1975; 39th Amendment and Article 329A(4); Khanna J strikes down clause 4 for violating free and fair elections, part of basic structure; refers to 'majority view of seven learned Judges' in Kesavananda

sources.name: Minerva Mills Ltd v Union of India, 31 July 1980
sources.what: Sections 4 and 55 of 42nd Amendment void; Article 368(4) and (5) struck down; limited amending power is a basic feature; Kesavananda majority ratio stated

sources.name: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v Union of India, 16 October 2015
sources.what: Constitution (Ninety-ninth Amendment) Act 2014 and NJAC Act declared unconstitutional and void

sources.name: Dr Balram Singh v Union of India, 25 November 2024, 2024 INSC 893
sources.what: Bench of CJI Sanjiv Khanna and Sanjay Kumar J dismissed challenge to 'socialist' and 'secular' in Preamble; amending power extends to Preamble; amendments can be challenged for basic structure violation; secularism a basic feature per earlier Constitution Benches

q.en: Which case first held that Parliament cannot amend the basic structure of the Constitution?
q.hi: किस मामले में पहली बार कहा गया कि संसद संविधान के मूल ढांचे का संशोधन नहीं कर सकती?

why.en: Kesavananda Bharati, 1973. Golaknath said fundamental rights could not be amended at all; Shankari Prasad upheld the First Amendment.
why.hi: केशवानंद भारती, 1973। गोलकनाथ ने कहा था कि मौलिक अधिकारों का संशोधन ही नहीं हो सकता; शंकरी प्रसाद ने पहले संशोधन को सही ठहराया था।

q.en: What did the Court hold in Golaknath, 1967?
q.hi: 1967 के गोलकनाथ मामले में अदालत ने क्या कहा?

en: Parliament can amend even the basic structure
Fundamental rights cannot be abridged by amendment
hi: संशोधन अनुच्छेद 13 के दायरे से बाहर हैं
संसद मूल ढांचे का भी संशोधन कर सकती है
संशोधन से मौलिक अधिकार कम नहीं किए जा सकते

why.en: Six of eleven judges treated an amendment as 'law' under Article 13.
why.hi: ग्यारह में से छह न्यायाधीशों ने संशोधन को अनुच्छेद 13 के अर्थ में कानून माना।

q.en: In Minerva Mills, 1980, what did the Court strike down?
q.hi: 1980 के मिनर्वा मिल्स मामले में अदालत ने क्या रद्द किया?

en: The rule on ratification by the States

why.en: A limited amending power is itself a basic feature. Article 329A(4) fell earlier, in Raj Narain, 1975.
why.hi: सीमित संशोधन शक्ति अपने आप में मूल ढांचे का तत्व है। अनुच्छेद 329क का खंड 4 पहले ही, 1975 के राज नारायण मामले में, रद्द हो चुका था।

factsToCheck: Kesavananda Bharati majority described as 'seven judges' on the basis of the Raj Narain judgment's wording; the 7:6 split and the signed summary of the majority view were not found in the opened text, so '7 to 6' is not said in the script

Raj Narain: the script says 'the Court struck down clause four' of Article 329A; Khanna J's holding (free and fair elections) and Chandrachud J's holding (clauses 4 and 5 void) were read, and Minerva Mills follows Raj Narain, but the count of judges on this point was not checked
Kesavananda as the largest bench ever, the name of the petitioner's math, and Minerva Mills' location were left out (not opened)
Legislative Department's own Constitution PDF could not be opened (page is script-rendered); Article 368 text taken from Indian Kanoon instead
notes: Teaches the legitimacy of the basic structure doctrine as contested (critics: not in the text, judge-defined, open-ended; supporters: needed guard for a limited amending power), without naming any person or party. Recall tests only settled holdings. The past question is quoted verbatim in English; the Hindi script gives its gist, flagged as such ('प्रश्न का भाव'), because pyq.json has no Hindi text. Recent example: Balram Singh v Union of India, 25 November 2024. Script notes that Article 368(4) and (5) still appear in printed texts though void after Minerva Mills.
